title: Missing authentication on a sensitive endpoint
description: An entry point that changes data, handles credentials/roles/payments/uploads, or returns user/order/admin data has no authentication guard (after applying global guards).
impact: Anyone on the network can call a function that should only be available to signed-in users.
remediation: Require authentication for the route (or deny by default globally) and allow-list only the intentionally public routes.
false_positive_guards: login/signup/password-reset-request/health/webhook-with-signature routes are allow-listed via config
global default-authentication settings are applied first
public catalogue reads are de-escalated

title: Privileged action without a role or ownership check
description: An authenticated entry point performs an admin-like action, or sibling routes enforce a role that this one does not.
impact: Any signed-in user can perform actions meant for administrators.
remediation: Add a role/permission guard (or an object-level policy) and test it with a non-privileged account.
false_positive_guards: inline role checks inside the handler count as a role check
routes behind an admin-only router guard are skipped

title: Caller identity or role taken from request data
description: A user id, owner id or role read from the body/query/headers/cookies is used for lookup, update or an authorization decision instead of the verified token/session. Includes guards that decide using request-supplied identity.
impact: An attacker can act as any user or claim any role by changing a request field.
remediation: Derive the caller's id and role only from the verified token or server-side session.
fix_example: const userId = req.user.id; // set by the verified auth middleware, never from req.body
false_positive_guards: route parameters naming the target object are handled by the IDOR rule
verified identity expressions (req.user, session, current_user) are never flagged

title: Object accessed by request-supplied id without ownership check
description: A lookup, update or delete uses an id from the request with no owner/tenant filter and no ownership comparison.
impact: A signed-in user can read or change other users' records by changing an id.
remediation: Scope every query by the authenticated user (owner/tenant) or verify ownership before acting.
fix_example: const doc = await Order.findOne({ _id: req.params.id, owner: req.user.id })
false_positive_guards: a filter key carrying the verified identity scopes the query
an ownership comparison or policy call in the handler suppresses the rule
admin-only routes are skipped

title: Privilege escalation through role assignment or mass assignment
description: A privileged role is granted in a registration path, a role/permission field is assigned from request data, or a whole request body is bound to a model that has privileged fields.
impact: Anyone can make themselves an administrator.
remediation: Set roles on the server only; bind requests to an explicit allow-list of fields.
fix_example: const { name, email, password } = req.body; await User.create({ name, email, password, role: 'user' })
false_positive_guards: pick/omit/permit allow-lists remove the taint
literal default roles such as 'user' are not privileged

title: Authorization guard fails open
description: A guard writes an error response (or swallows an exception) but a path still reaches the protected code.
impact: The check can be bypassed, so the protected routes are effectively public.
remediation: Return or throw immediately after denying; never call next()/proceed from an error path.
false_positive_guards: return/throw right after the deny response ends the path
next(err) in an error callback that returns is not a proceed

title: Guard does not cover every route it should
description: A guard applies only to some HTTP methods, is registered after the routes it should protect, or admin paths sit outside the guarded prefix.
impact: Some routes (other methods, earlier routes, admin paths) are reachable without the check.
remediation: Register guards before routes, apply them to all methods, and guard whole prefixes.
false_positive_guards: routes that are intentionally public are skipped

title: Request data reaches a file API without containment
description: Request data reaches a file read/write/delete/send/extract API with no normalisation and base-directory check (includes zip-slip).
impact: An attacker can read, overwrite or delete arbitrary files on the server.
remediation: Resolve the path, verify it stays inside the base directory, or map ids to files.
fix_example: const p = path.resolve(BASE, name); if (!p.startsWith(BASE + path.sep)) return res.sendStatus(400)
false_positive_guards: basename()/secure_filename() sanitise
a startsWith/is_relative_to containment check in the handler suppresses the rule

title: Server-side request forgery
description: Request data chooses the URL or host of a server-side HTTP client, URL fetcher or renderer with no allow-list.
impact: An attacker can make the server call internal services or cloud metadata endpoints.
remediation: Allow-list schemes and hosts, resolve and block private/link-local ranges, disable blind redirects.
false_positive_guards: a fixed scheme+host prefix means only the path is user-controlled
an allow-list/validation condition on the value suppresses the rule

title: Open redirect
description: Request data is used as a redirect location without an allow-list.
impact: Attackers can send victims to phishing sites through a trusted domain.
remediation: Redirect only to relative paths or allow-listed hosts.
false_positive_guards: a fixed relative prefix is safe
an allow-list check on the value suppresses the rule

title: State-changing cookie/session-authenticated route without CSRF protection
description: A state-changing route authenticated by cookie or session has no CSRF token, SameSite or Origin check, or CSRF protection is explicitly disabled.
impact: A malicious site can make a signed-in victim's browser perform actions.
remediation: Enable CSRF tokens (or SameSite=Lax/Strict plus Origin checks) for session-authenticated routes.
false_positive_guards: Django/Spring/Rails/Laravel enable CSRF by default: only explicit disabling is flagged
bearer-token-only APIs are not cookie authenticated

title: CORS misconfiguration
description: Reflected Origin, wildcard origin with credentials, over-broad origin patterns, or default permissive CORS on an authenticated API.
impact: Any website can read authenticated responses from the API in a victim's browser.
remediation: Allow-list exact origins; never combine wildcard/reflected origins with credentials.
false_positive_guards: wildcard without credentials on an unauthenticated API is low severity

title: Sensitive fields or whole collections returned without restriction
description: A response is built from a whole model object or collection that has sensitive fields (password hash, token, secret) without projection, or a serializer exposes all fields.
impact: Credential hashes, tokens or other users' data are disclosed to callers.
remediation: Project explicit safe fields (DTO/serializer allow-list) and restrict collection endpoints by role.
false_positive_guards: select/exclude/values/only projections suppress the rule
models without sensitive fields are not flagged

title: Dangerous permission or exposure default
description: World-writable permissions, the project root or sensitive files served statically, directory listing, or backup/config/.env files inside web-served directories.
impact: Local users or remote visitors can modify or download files that should be private.
remediation: Use restrictive modes (0o600/0o750), serve a dedicated public directory, and keep secrets and backups out of it.
false_positive_guards: conventional public directories are only flagged when they contain sensitive file names

title: Role check exists only in client-side code
description: Front-end code hides or shows features by role, and the server endpoints it calls have no matching server-side role check. Supporting evidence for the server-side finding.
impact: Hiding a button does not stop a user calling the endpoint directly.
remediation: Enforce the same role check on the server; treat client checks as UX only.
false_positive_guards: only reported when a matching server endpoint lacks a role guard
never reported above low severity

title: Token or session identity weakness
description: Tokens issued without an expiry, tokens decoded without verification and used as identity, or a single static API key used as the only access control.
impact: Stolen or forged tokens stay valid forever or are accepted without proof.
remediation: Verify signatures, set short expiries, and use scoped, rotatable credentials.
false_positive_guards: expiresIn/exp present means no finding
